title: Hiking Pace Calculator: Minutes per Mile and km
description: Convert hike distance and time into pace and average speed with the Hiking Pace Calculator — min per mile and per kilometre. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, 8 miles in 3 hours 20 minutes is a 25:00-per-mile pace (2.4 mph) — the relaxed hill-walking speed the maths insists on.
quick_answer: The Hiking Pace Calculator converts distance and duration into pace — minutes per mile and per kilometre — and average speed. Enter the distance and the time and read the figures your next route plan should be built from, because planned pace and actual pace are rarely introduced.

A group's pace is its slowest member's comfortable pace. Measure it on a short walk before the long one depends on it.
Same trail, falling minutes-per-mile: the log that proves fitness arrived. Pace is the trail's stopwatch-readable truth.
Your flat pace versus your hill pace, both measured, is the personal correction factor every guidebook estimate needs.
8 miles in 3 h 20 min: pace = 200 ÷ 8 = 25:00/mile; speed = 8 ÷ 3.333 = 2.4 mph. A walker who assumed 3 mph would plan this trail an hour short — the measurement prevents exactly that.

faq: Does this replace a specialist tool or professional measurement?
No — it divides distance by time, exactly. GPS watches add elevation and splits; this is the transparent core they must agree with.
Is my input uploaded?
No. Distance and time are computed in your browser.
Does the route include live traffic?
No — trails have weather and stiles instead of traffic, and both live inside your measured time already.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Trails wind more than roads. Enter the trail distance you actually walked, from the route or your device.
Can route results change over time?
Your pace will, with fitness and season. Recompute from recent walks; plan with the current walker.
Moving pace or elapsed pace?
Elapsed includes the viewpoint stops — plan days with elapsed, judge fitness with moving. Enter the time that matches your question.
How does ascent change pace?
Climbing slows the horizontal pace; Naismith adds time for height separately. The Hiking Route Planner applies the full rule to a real route.
Pace with a heavy pack?
Slower, and measurably so — which is the point of measuring it. Multi-day plans deserve the loaded figure from a loaded test walk.
Children in the party?
The party's pace is the children's exploring pace, which includes stops for everything interesting. Measure it on a family walk, not from your solo logs.
Poles and terrain change pace?
Yes — scrambling, bog and scree all tax pace in ways flat arithmetic notices only through your measured time. Measure on similar ground.
